programmes.amount_note: Monthly allotment on an EBT card depends on household size, income and deductions; FY2026 maximum allotments are published by USDA FNS

procedure_steps.detail: Apply with your state SNAP agency (online in most states)
Complete an eligibility interview (usually by phone)
Receive EBT card and monthly benefits if approved (within 30 days; expedited in 7 days)

eligibility.income_note: Gross monthly income generally at or below 130% of the federal poverty level; net income at or below 100% FPL; many states use higher limits via broad-based categorical eligibility

programmes.source_snippet: USDA FNS administers SNAP; households must meet income limits and apply through their state agency.

programmes.name_local: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC)
programmes.name_en: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC)
programmes.amount_note: Monthly food package value varies by participant category (pregnant/postpartum/breastfeeding women, infants, children)

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your local or state WIC agency to schedule an appointment
Attend a certification appointment with a free health/nutrition assessment
Receive eWIC card for WIC-approved foods if eligible

documents_required.doc: Proof of income or participation in Medicaid/SNAP/TANF

eligibility.income_note: Income at or below 185% of the federal poverty level, or adjunct eligibility via Medicaid, SNAP or TANF

programmes.source_snippet: WIC is available for women who are currently pregnant, recently pregnant, or breastfeeding, and babies and kids under 5.

programmes.name_local: National School Lunch Program (NSLP) and School Breakfast Program (SBP)
programmes.name_en: National School Lunch Program and School Breakfast Program
programmes.amount_note: Free or reduced-price meals at school; reduced price is capped at $0.40 for lunch and $0.30 for breakfast

procedure_steps.detail: Ask your child's school for a free/reduced-price meal application (or check if the school serves free meals to all under CEP)
Submit household income application to the school nutrition office
Children in SNAP/TANF households are directly certified for free meals

eligibility.income_note: Free meals at or below 130% of the federal poverty level; reduced-price meals between 130% and 185% FPL

programmes.source_snippet: Students from households with incomes at or below 130 percent of the Federal poverty line can receive a free lunch; between 130 and 185 percent a reduced-price lunch.

programmes.amount_note: $120 per eligible school-age child for the summer (2024-2025 standard amount), loaded on an EBT card
programmes.deadline_note: Administered by states during the summer months; many families are automatically enrolled

procedure_steps.detail: Check whether your state operates SUN Bucks and whether you are automatically enrolled
If not automatic, apply through your state SUN Bucks portal
Receive $120 per child on an EBT card for summer groceries

documents_required.doc: Child enrollment in a school with free/reduced-price meals or household participation in SNAP/TANF

eligibility.income_note: Children eligible for free/reduced-price school meals or in households receiving SNAP, TANF or FDPIR

programmes.source_snippet: SUN Bucks provides grocery-buying benefits to eligible school-aged children during the summer when schools are closed.

programmes.amount_note: Free USDA foods distributed through food banks, pantries and soup kitchens; no cash value to recipients

procedure_steps.detail: Find a local food bank or pantry distributing TEFAP foods
Self-declare income eligibility or show participation in other assistance programs, per state rules

eligibility.income_note: Income limits set by each state, typically tied to a percentage of the federal poverty level or participation in SNAP/other programs

programmes.source_snippet: TEFAP provides USDA foods to low-income Americans through food banks and emergency feeding organizations.

programmes.amount_note: Monthly package of nutritious USDA foods

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your state or local CSFP agency
Apply and show age and income eligibility
Pick up a monthly food package

eligibility.income_note: Adults 60+ with income at or below 130% of the federal poverty level (state rules apply)

programmes.source_snippet: CSFP works to improve the health of low-income persons at least 60 years of age by supplementing their diets with nutritious USDA foods.

programmes.amount_note: Seasonal coupons/vouchers for fresh produce at farmers' markets; benefit level set by each state
programmes.deadline_note: Seasonal (growing season); coupons issued until funds run out

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your state SFMNP agency or local aging office
Apply and receive coupons
Redeem at authorized farmers' markets and roadside stands

eligibility.income_note: Adults 60+ (55+ in some tribal programs) with income at or below 185% of the federal poverty level

programmes.source_snippet: SFMNP provides low-income seniors with coupons that can be exchanged for eligible foods at farmers' markets, roadside stands, and community supported agriculture programs.

programmes.funder: U.S. HHS Administration for Children and Families (ACF)
programmes.amount_note: Monthly cash benefit amount and rules are set by each state; federal lifetime limit of 60 months for adult recipients

procedure_steps.detail: Apply at your state or county social services agency (each state runs its own TANF program)
Complete an interview and provide income/family documentation
Participate in required work activities to keep benefits

eligibility.income_note: Very low income; each state sets its own income and resource limits; work requirements and a 60-month federal time limit apply

programmes.source_snippet: TANF provides states with flexible funding for programs aimed at promoting stability, family preservation, and access to employment among low-income households with children.

programmes.amount_note: 2026 federal benefit rate: up to $994/month individual and $1,491/month couple; reduced by countable income; many states add a supplement

procedure_steps.detail: Start an application online, by phone (1-800-772-1213) or at a local Social Security office
Provide medical evidence (if under 65 and claiming disability) and financial information
SSA decides; payments begin the month after approval

eligibility.income_note: Aged 65+, blind or disabled with very limited income (below the federal benefit rate after exclusions) and resources at or below $2,000 individual / $3,000 couple

programmes.source_snippet: In 2026, the maximum federal SSI payment rose to $994 per month for an eligible individual and $1,491 for an eligible couple, reflecting the 2.8 percent cost-of-living adjustment.

programmes.amount_note: Monthly benefit is based on your lifetime earnings record; Medicare eligibility begins after 24 months of SSDI entitlement

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online at ssa.gov/disability, by phone 1-800-772-1213, or at a local office
Submit medical records and work history
State Disability Determination Services reviews the claim; appeals available if denied

documents_required.doc: Social Security number and birth record
Work history for the last 15 years

eligibility.income_note: Must meet SSA's disability definition and have enough Social Security work credits (generally 40 credits, 20 in the last 10 years)

programmes.source_snippet: Social Security pays disability benefits through 2 programs: Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI).

programmes.amount_note: Monthly benefit depends on lifetime earnings and claiming age (62-70); average retired-worker benefit is about $2,000/month in 2026

procedure_steps.detail: Create a my Social Security account to see your estimate
Apply online up to 4 months before you want benefits to start
Choose when to claim between age 62 and 70

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested; requires about 10 years (40 credits) of work paying Social Security taxes

programmes.source_snippet: You can start receiving Social Security retirement benefits as early as age 62, but benefits are reduced before full retirement age.

programmes.amount_note: Monthly payment tops up countable income to the Maximum Annual Pension Rate (MAPR); higher rates with Aid and Attendance or Housebound

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility (wartime service, age 65+ or totally disabled, income/net worth limits)
File VA Form 21P-527EZ online, by mail or with a Veterans Service Officer
VA reviews income and service records and sets the pension rate

eligibility.income_note: Wartime veterans with limited income and net worth below the VA limit; age 65+ or permanently and totally disabled

programmes.source_snippet: The Veterans Pension program provides monthly payments to wartime Veterans who meet certain age or disability requirements, and who have income and net worth within certain limits.

programmes.funder: U.S. Department of Labor / state workforce agencies
programmes.amount_note: Weekly benefit amount, duration (typically up to 26 weeks) and rules are set by each state based on prior wages

procedure_steps.detail: File a claim with the unemployment office of the state where you worked, as soon as you lose your job
Certify weekly and report any earnings
Meet work-search requirements to keep benefits

documents_required.doc: Employment history for the last 18 months

eligibility.income_note: Must have lost work through no fault of your own and earned enough wages in the base period; must be able and available to work

programmes.source_snippet: Unemployment Insurance provides temporary financial assistance to eligible workers who lost their jobs through no fault of their own; claims are filed with the state unemployment agency.

programmes.name_local: WIOA Adult and Dislocated Worker Programs
programmes.name_en: Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) Career Services and Training
programmes.funder: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration
programmes.amount_note: Free career services and training funding (Individual Training Accounts) delivered through American Job Centers

procedure_steps.detail: Visit or contact your local American Job Center
Meet with a career counselor to assess eligibility and needs
Enroll in training or job-search services funded by WIOA

documents_required.doc: Proof of identity and work authorization
Layoff notice or proof of income (priority groups)

eligibility.income_note: Adults 18+; priority for individualized and training services goes to low-income individuals, public benefit recipients and dislocated workers

programmes.source_snippet: WIOA funds employment and training services for adults, dislocated workers and youth through a nationwide network of American Job Centers.

programmes.amount_note: Free residential career training, education, housing, meals and a basic living allowance for eligible young people

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online or at an admissions office
Meet with an admissions counselor and provide documents
Enroll at a Job Corps center for career technical training

eligibility.income_note: Low-income youth ages 16-24 (no upper age limit for applicants with disabilities)

programmes.source_snippet: Job Corps is the nation's largest free residential education and job training program for young adults ages 16-24.

programmes.amount_note: Trade Readjustment Allowances (income support during training), training costs, job search and relocation allowances
programmes.deadline_note: Only for workers covered by a certified DOL petition; file through your state workforce agency

procedure_steps.detail: Check if your employer's worker group has a certified TAA petition
Apply through your state workforce agency / American Job Center
Enroll in approved training to receive income support

documents_required.doc: Proof of employment and layoff from the certified employer

eligibility.income_note: Workers who lost their jobs due to foreign trade, covered by a certified petition

programmes.source_snippet: TAA provides assistance to workers who have lost their jobs as a result of increased imports or shifts in production outside the United States.

programmes.amount_note: Free vocational rehabilitation, training, job placement and benefits counseling for disability beneficiaries who want to work

procedure_steps.detail: Call the Ticket to Work Help Line or find a service provider online
Assign your Ticket to an Employment Network or state VR agency
Receive work incentives planning and employment services

eligibility.income_note: SSDI and SSI disability beneficiaries ages 18-64; voluntary and free

programmes.source_snippet: The Ticket to Work program supports career development for Social Security disability beneficiaries ages 18 through 64 who want to work.

programmes.amount_note: Tax year 2025 maximum credit: $649 (no children) to $8,046 (3+ children); income must be under $61,555 (single/HOH) or $68,675 (married filing jointly); refundable
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed on your annual federal tax return (Form 1040, Schedule EIC); refunds issued after mid-February by law

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility with the IRS EITC Assistant
File Form 1040 (with Schedule EIC if you have qualifying children)
Receive the credit as part of your tax refund

documents_required.doc: Valid SSNs for filer, spouse and qualifying children

eligibility.income_note: Low-to-moderate earned income; TY2025 AGI limits range from $19,104 (single, no children) to $68,675 (married filing jointly, 3+ children); investment income must be $11,950 or less

programmes.source_snippet: If you earned less than $68,675 (Married Filing Jointly) or $61,555 (Single, Qualifying Surviving Spouse or Head of Household) in tax year 2025, you may qualify for the Earned Income Credit.

programmes.amount_note: Up to $2,200 per qualifying child under 17 for tax year 2025 (made permanent and inflation-indexed by the 2025 tax law); partially refundable up to $1,700 via the Additional Child Tax Credit
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed on the annual federal income tax return

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm each child has a valid SSN and meets age/relationship/residency tests
File Form 1040 and complete the Child Tax Credit worksheet
Refundable portion (ACTC) arrives with your refund

eligibility.income_note: Phases out at higher incomes ($200,000 single / $400,000 married filing jointly); child must be under 17 at year end

programmes.source_snippet: The Child Tax Credit provides a credit of up to $2,200 per qualifying child under age 17 for tax year 2025.

programmes.amount_note: Credit of 50%, 20% or 10% of up to $2,000 ($4,000 if married filing jointly) contributed to a retirement plan or IRA; maximum credit $1,000 ($2,000 MFJ); non-refundable
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed on the annual federal tax return (Form 8880)

procedure_steps.detail: Contribute to a 401(k), IRA or similar plan during the year
Check your AGI against the Saver's Credit rate table
File Form 8880 with your Form 1040

eligibility.income_note: AGI below the annual thresholds (around $79,000 MFJ / $59,250 HOH / $39,500 single for 2025); cannot be a full-time student or claimed as a dependent

programmes.source_snippet: The Saver's Credit is a tax credit for eligible contributions to retirement plans; the credit rate is 50%, 20% or 10% of contributions depending on adjusted gross income.

programmes.amount_note: Up to $2,500 per eligible student per year for the first 4 years of higher education; 40% (up to $1,000) is refundable
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed on the annual tax return (Form 8863) using Form 1098-T from the school

procedure_steps.detail: Obtain Form 1098-T from the eligible educational institution
Keep receipts for tuition, fees and course materials
File Form 8863 with your Form 1040

eligibility.income_note: Phases out for MAGI between $80,000-$90,000 ($160,000-$180,000 MFJ); student must be enrolled at least half-time in a degree program and not have completed 4 years of higher education

programmes.source_snippet: The American Opportunity Tax Credit is a credit for qualified education expenses paid for an eligible student for the first four years of higher education, up to $2,500 per eligible student.

programmes.amount_note: 20% of the first $10,000 of qualified tuition and fees, up to $2,000 per tax return per year; non-refundable; no limit on number of years
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed on the annual tax return (Form 8863)

procedure_steps.detail: Obtain Form 1098-T from the school
Total qualified tuition and related expenses
File Form 8863 with your Form 1040

documents_required.doc: Payment records for tuition and fees

eligibility.income_note: Phases out for MAGI between $80,000-$90,000 ($160,000-$180,000 MFJ); available for undergraduate, graduate and job-skills courses

programmes.source_snippet: The Lifetime Learning Credit is worth up to $2,000 per tax return for qualified tuition and related expenses at eligible educational institutions.

programmes.name_local: IRS Free File and VITA Free Tax Preparation
programmes.name_en: IRS Free File / Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA)
programmes.amount_note: Free tax preparation and e-filing; ensures low-income filers claim EITC, CTC and other credits without paying preparer fees
programmes.deadline_note: Tax season (January-April 15); VITA/TCE sites operate locally

procedure_steps.detail: Use IRS Free File if your AGI is within the limit, or find a VITA site
Bring ID, SSNs and income documents to the VITA site (or file online)
IRS-certified volunteers prepare and e-file your return for free

eligibility.income_note: VITA generally serves people earning $67,000 or less, persons with disabilities and limited English speakers; IRS Free File guided software is free below an AGI threshold

programmes.source_snippet: VITA and TCE sites offer free basic tax return preparation to qualified individuals, generally people who make $67,000 or less, persons with disabilities and limited English-speaking taxpayers.

programmes.funder: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) / state Medicaid agencies
programmes.amount_note: Free or very low-cost comprehensive health coverage; enrollees pay little or nothing for covered services

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through your state Medicaid agency or via HealthCare.gov (one application screens Medicaid, CHIP and Marketplace savings)
Provide household, income and identity information
Enroll with a state Medicaid plan; renew annually

documents_required.doc: Proof of identity and citizenship/immigration status

programmes.source_snippet: Medicaid provides health coverage to millions of Americans, including eligible low-income adults, children, pregnant women, elderly adults and people with disabilities.

programmes.funder: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) / states
programmes.amount_note: Low-cost coverage for children; some states charge small premiums or copays capped by federal law

procedure_steps.detail: Apply any time of year through your state or HealthCare.gov
If income is too high for Medicaid, children are routed to CHIP
Choose a CHIP plan and pay any small state premium

documents_required.doc: Child's proof of age and identity

eligibility.income_note: Children under 19 in families with income too high for Medicaid but below the state's CHIP limit, which ranges from about 170% to 400% of the federal poverty level by state

programmes.name_en: Advance Premium Tax Credit for Marketplace Health Insurance
programmes.funder: Internal Revenue Service (IRS) / Health Insurance Marketplace
programmes.amount_note: Credit caps your benchmark silver-plan premium at a percentage of household income; paid in advance directly to the insurer or claimed at tax time
programmes.deadline_note: Annual Open Enrollment (typically Nov 1-Jan 15) plus Special Enrollment Periods after qualifying life events

Estimate household income for the coverage year
Choose how much of the credit to take in advance and pick a plan
Reconcile the credit on Form 8962 with your tax return

documents_required.doc: Income estimate and prior tax return

eligibility.income_note: Household income generally at least 100% of the federal poverty level; credit amount slides with income and is reconciled on the tax return; not available with an affordable employer offer or Medicaid

programmes.source_snippet: When you apply for Marketplace coverage, you'll find out if you qualify for a premium tax credit that lowers your monthly premium.

programmes.deadline_note: Available only on Silver plans during Marketplace enrollment periods

If eligible, choose a Silver plan to get the extra savings
Savings apply automatically to the Silver plan's cost sharing

programmes.source_snippet: If your income qualifies, you can get extra savings on out-of-pocket costs like deductibles and copayments — but only if you enroll in a Silver plan.

procedure_steps.detail: Sign up through Social Security online, by phone or in person
Choose Original Medicare or a Medicare Advantage plan
Add Part D drug coverage or a Medigap policy if desired

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested; for people 65+, certain younger people with disabilities, and people with End-Stage Renal Disease

programmes.source_snippet: Medicare is federal health insurance for people 65 or older, and some people under 65 with certain disabilities or conditions.

programmes.name_en: Extra Help with Medicare Prescription Drug Costs
programmes.amount_note: Worth an estimated $5,700 per year; enrollees pay no Part D premium/deductible and modest copays (no more than $12.65 brand-name / $5.10 generic in 2026)

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online at ssa.gov/extrahelp, by phone or at a local SSA office (automatic if you have Medicaid, SSI or a Medicare Savings Program)
Provide income and resource information
SSA mails a decision; then enroll in a Part D plan

eligibility.income_note: Medicare beneficiaries with income below 150% of the federal poverty level and resources at or below $17,600 (single) / $35,130 (couple) in 2025

programmes.source_snippet: Medicare Part D Extra Help is a program that covers some of the Part D prescription drug plan costs; its estimated average annual value is $5,700 per person.

programmes.amount_note: Pays the Medicare Part B premium (and, under QMB, deductibles and coinsurance); worth at least the Part B premium per month

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through your state Medicaid office (each state runs these programs)
Provide income and resource information
State notifies you and the premium savings appear on your Medicare/Social Security record

eligibility.income_note: Medicare beneficiaries with limited income and resources; QMB, SLMB and QI have different income ceilings set as percentages of the federal poverty level

programmes.source_snippet: Medicare Savings Programs help pay Medicare premiums and in some cases deductibles, coinsurance and copayments for people with limited income and resources.

programmes.funder: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) / local Public Housing Agencies
programmes.amount_note: PHA pays the landlord the difference between about 30% of household income and the rent up to a local payment standard

procedure_steps.detail: Find your local Public Housing Agency (PHA) and join the waiting list when open
When selected, attend a briefing and receive a voucher
Find a qualifying unit; PHA inspects it and pays its share of rent to the landlord

documents_required.doc: Proof of identity and citizenship/eligible immigration status
Income verification for all household members

eligibility.income_note: Income generally at or below 50% of area median income; 75% of new vouchers must go to households at or below 30% of area median income or the poverty line

programmes.funder: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) / local Public Housing Agencies
programmes.amount_note: Rent is generally capped at about 30% of adjusted household income in PHA-owned apartments

procedure_steps.detail: Apply at your local Public Housing Agency
Join the waiting list for available units
Sign a lease for a PHA-owned unit when offered

eligibility.income_note: Low-income families, seniors and people with disabilities; income limits at 80% of area median income (lower limits apply to most admissions)

programmes.source_snippet: Public housing provides decent and safe rental housing for eligible low-income families, the elderly, and persons with disabilities.

programmes.name_local: Single Family Housing Direct Home Loans (Section 502)
programmes.name_en: USDA Section 502 Direct Home Loan Program
programmes.amount_note: Payment assistance (subsidy) reduces the effective mortgage interest rate for low- and very-low-income buyers in eligible rural areas

procedure_steps.detail: Check that the property is in an eligible rural area and your income is within limits
Apply through your local USDA Rural Development office
Complete homebuyer requirements and close on the home

eligibility.income_note: Low and very low income (generally below 80% of area median income) for homes in eligible rural areas; must be unable to obtain credit elsewhere

programmes.source_snippet: Section 502 direct loans assist low- and very-low-income applicants obtain decent, safe and sanitary housing in eligible rural areas with payment assistance that increases repayment ability.

programmes.name_local: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)
programmes.funder: U.S. HHS Administration for Children and Families (ACF)
programmes.amount_note: Benefit amount, season and crisis assistance rules are set by each state/territory/tribe; payments usually go directly to the utility or fuel vendor
programmes.deadline_note: Application windows vary by state; crisis assistance available year-round in many states

Apply with proof of income and energy bills
Benefit is paid to your utility or fuel provider

procedure_steps.detail: Identify and contact your state weatherization administrator or local Community Action Agency
Apply with proof of income
Receive a free energy audit and weatherization work

documents_required.doc: Proof of homeownership or landlord permission (renters)

eligibility.income_note: Households at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines or receiving SSI; priority for seniors, people with disabilities and families with children

programmes.source_snippet: Households that fall at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines or receive Supplemental Security Income (SSI) are eligible for weatherization assistance; services are 100% free for those who qualify.

programmes.amount_note: Up to $9.25/month off phone, internet or bundled service; up to $34.25/month for consumers on qualifying Tribal lands; one discount per household

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility and apply through the National Verifier at lifelinesupport.org
Choose a participating phone or internet company
Recertify every year to keep the benefit

documents_required.doc: Proof of income or program participation (SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, etc.)

eligibility.income_note: Income at or below 135% of the federal poverty guidelines, or participation in SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance, Veterans Pension or certain Tribal programs

programmes.source_snippet: Qualifying consumers can get a monthly discount of up to $9.25 off the cost of their phone, internet, or bundled services. Consumers living on qualifying Tribal lands can get up to $34.25 per month.

programmes.funder: U.S. Department of Education, Federal Student Aid
programmes.amount_note: Award ranges from $740 to $7,395 for 2025-26 and 2026-27, based on Student Aid Index, cost of attendance and enrollment intensity; does not have to be repaid

procedure_steps.detail: Complete the FAFSA at studentaid.gov
Review your FAFSA Submission Summary / Student Aid Index
The school's financial aid office applies the Pell Grant to your account

documents_required.doc: Federal tax information (transferred via IRS data)

eligibility.income_note: Undergraduates with exceptional financial need (no prior bachelor's degree); maximum award generally for household income below 175% of federal poverty guidelines (225% for single-parent households)

programmes.source_snippet: For both the 2025-26 and 2026-27 award years, the maximum Pell Grant award is $7,395; eligible students can receive between $740 and $7,395.

programmes.funder: U.S. Department of Education, Federal Student Aid
programmes.amount_note: $100 to $4,000 per year depending on need, other aid received, and the school's FSEOG funds; priority to Pell Grant recipients with the lowest Student Aid Index
programmes.deadline_note: File the FAFSA early; each school has a limited FSEOG allocation

procedure_steps.detail: File the FAFSA
Attend a participating school; the financial aid office awards FSEOG to the neediest students first
Funds are credited to your student account

eligibility.income_note: Undergraduates with exceptional financial need; not all schools participate

programmes.source_snippet: FSEOG awards range from $100 to $4,000 a year; priority is given to students with the greatest financial need who also receive Pell Grants.

programmes.funder: U.S. Department of Education, Federal Student Aid

Accept the Work-Study award from your school
Find an approved on- or off-campus job and earn up to your award

eligibility.income_note: Undergraduate and graduate students with financial need at participating schools

programmes.source_snippet: Federal Work-Study provides part-time jobs for undergraduate and graduate students with financial need, allowing them to earn money to help pay education expenses.

programmes.funder: U.S. Department of Education, Federal Student Aid
programmes.amount_note: Forgives the entire remaining balance on Direct Loans after 120 qualifying monthly payments (10 years) while working full-time for a qualifying public-service employer; forgiven amount is not federally taxed

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm your employer qualifies with the PSLF Help Tool
Submit the PSLF Employment Certification Form annually
Make 120 qualifying payments on a Direct Loan under a qualifying plan, then apply for forgiveness

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested; requires Direct Loans, full-time work for government or a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, and 120 qualifying payments

programmes.source_snippet: PSLF forgives the remaining balance on your Direct Loans after you have made 120 qualifying monthly payments under a qualifying repayment plan while working full-time for a qualifying employer.

programmes.name_local: Head Start and Early Head Start
programmes.funder: U.S. HHS Administration for Children and Families, Office of Head Start
programmes.amount_note: Free early childhood education, health, nutrition and family services for children from birth to age 5 and pregnant women

procedure_steps.detail: Find a local Head Start program using the Head Start Center Locator
Apply with proof of income and child's age
Program enrolls the child; priority to children in foster care, homelessness and public-assistance families

documents_required.doc: Proof of income or program participation (TANF/SNAP/SSI)

eligibility.income_note: Family income at or below the federal poverty level, or children in foster care, homeless families, or families receiving public assistance; programs may serve some families up to 130% of poverty

programmes.source_snippet: Head Start programs promote school readiness of infants, toddlers, and preschool-aged children from low-income families through education, health and family services.

programmes.name_local: Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF) Subsidies
programmes.funder: U.S. HHS Administration for Children and Families, Office of Child Care
programmes.amount_note: Subsidy covers all or most of child care costs; parents pay a sliding-scale copayment set by the state

procedure_steps.detail: Find your state or territory child care assistance office via childcare.gov
Apply and provide work/education and income information
Choose an eligible provider; subsidy is paid to the provider

documents_required.doc: Proof of income and work/school activity

eligibility.income_note: Children under 13 (older if disabled) in low-income working families; states set income limits within the federal ceiling of 85% of state median income

programmes.source_snippet: CCDF helps low-income families access child care so parents can work or attend education and training, administered by state, territory and tribal lead agencies.

programmes.name_local: Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP)
programmes.amount_note: Free or reduced-price nutritious meals and snacks served in child care centers, day care homes, after-school programs and adult day care

procedure_steps.detail: Enroll your child in a participating child care or after-school program
Complete the center's income eligibility form
Meals are served free or at reduced price at the site

documents_required.doc: Income eligibility form from the care provider

eligibility.income_note: Free meals at or below 130% of poverty; reduced price between 130% and 185% FPL; centers in low-income areas may serve free meals to all

programmes.source_snippet: CACFP provides aid to child and adult care institutions and family or group day care homes for the provision of nutritious foods.

programmes.amount_note: Access to set-aside and sole-source federal contracts plus business development assistance for up to 9 years; no direct cash grant

procedure_steps.detail: Create an account at certify.sba.gov and gather ownership/ financial documents
Submit the 8(a) application showing social and economic disadvantage
If certified, pursue set-aside federal contracts with SBA support

eligibility.income_note: Businesses at least 51% owned by socially and economically disadvantaged U.S. citizens; personal net worth under $850,000, AGI under $400,000 and assets under $6.5 million

programmes.source_snippet: The 8(a) program helps small businesses owned by socially and economically disadvantaged people compete for set-aside and sole-source federal contracts.

programmes.amount_note: Loans up to $50,000 (average about $13,000) through nonprofit intermediary lenders for small business startup and expansion; this is a repayable loan, not a grant

procedure_steps.detail: Find an SBA-approved intermediary microlender in your area
Apply with a business plan and financials
Receive funds (some intermediaries require training or collateral)

eligibility.income_note: For-profit small businesses, including many low-income entrepreneurs who cannot get conventional bank credit

programmes.source_snippet: The Microloan program provides loans up to $50,000 to help small businesses and certain not-for-profit childcare centers start up and expand.

programmes.amount_note: Refundable credit up to $3,756 for tax year 2025 depending on income and number of children ($302 with no children); stacks with federal EITC and Young Child Tax Credit
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed on the California income tax return with Form FTB 3514 (ITIN filers eligible)

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility with the FTB CalEITC calculator
File a California return and complete Form FTB 3514 (free via CalFile)
Receive the credit as a refund even if you owe no tax

eligibility.income_note: California residents with earned income up to about $32,900 (tax year 2025); ITIN filers are eligible

programmes.source_snippet: Under CalEITC, individuals and families earning less than $31,950 may qualify for a cash back tax credit; claim it with Form FTB 3514 on your state return.

programmes.amount_note: Refundable credit of up to about $1,189 per tax return (tax year 2025) for CalEITC-eligible families with a child under age 6
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed with Form FTB 3514 on the California tax return

procedure_steps.detail: File a California return with Form FTB 3514
Claim YCTC for each return with a qualifying child under 6
Refund issued even with zero tax liability

eligibility.income_note: Must qualify for CalEITC (or have zero income) with a child under age 6

programmes.source_snippet: The Young Child Tax Credit provides a credit of up to $1,189 per tax return for Californians who qualify for CalEITC and have a child under 6 years old.

programmes.amount_note: California's version of SNAP; monthly EBT allotment depends on household size and income

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online at BenefitsCal or at your county social services office
Complete a phone interview
Receive an EBT card if approved (expedited service within 3 days in emergencies)

eligibility.income_note: California households meeting SNAP income rules (generally up to 130% of poverty gross income, higher via categorical eligibility)

programmes.source_snippet: CalFresh, federally known as SNAP, issues monthly electronic benefits that can be used to buy most foods at many markets and food stores.

programmes.funder: California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS)
programmes.amount_note: Free or low-cost health coverage; most enrollees pay no premiums or copays

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via BenefitsCal, Covered California, or your county office
County determines eligibility
Choose a managed care plan in your county

eligibility.income_note: Adults up to 138% of the federal poverty level; higher limits for children and pregnant women; California covers eligible residents regardless of immigration status

programmes.source_snippet: Medi-Cal is California's Medicaid program, offering free or low-cost health coverage for children and adults with limited income and resources.

programmes.name_local: CalWORKs (California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids)
programmes.amount_note: Monthly cash aid amount depends on family size, income and county; recipients also get welfare-to-work services and child care

procedure_steps.detail: Apply at BenefitsCal or your county social services office
Complete an intake interview and eligibility determination
Participate in the welfare-to-work program while receiving cash aid

documents_required.doc: Proof of children's ages and school attendance

eligibility.income_note: Very low-income California families with children (also pregnant women); state/county income and resource limits apply

programmes.source_snippet: CalWORKs is California's TANF program providing cash aid and services to eligible needy California families with children.

programmes.funder: New York State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA)
programmes.amount_note: Regular benefit of up to $996 per season depending on heating type and income; separate Emergency, Heating Equipment Repair/Replacement and Cooling Assistance components
programmes.deadline_note: Regular benefit typically opens in early November/December and runs until funds are exhausted; emergency component opens in January

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online at myBenefits, by mail or at your local department of social services
Provide income, household and heating cost information
Benefit is paid directly to your utility or fuel vendor

eligibility.income_note: New York households within published HEAP income limits (tiered by household size); receipt of SNAP, TA or SSI can confer eligibility

programmes.source_snippet: Eligible households can receive up to $996 through the Regular HEAP benefit, depending on how they heat their home; payments go directly to your utility company or energy provider.

programmes.funder: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
programmes.amount_note: Refundable credit per qualifying child; expanded amounts for 2025 (up to $1,000 for children under 4 and $330 for children ages 4-16 for eligible filers)
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed on the New York State income tax return (Form IT-213)

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility on the Tax Department website
File a New York return with Form IT-213
Credit is refunded with your state refund

eligibility.income_note: New York residents with at least one qualifying child under 17 and federal child tax credit eligibility or income under state thresholds

programmes.source_snippet: The Empire State Child Credit is a refundable credit for New York taxpayers with qualifying children under age 17.

programmes.funder: New York State Higher Education Services Corporation (HESC)
programmes.amount_note: Covers remaining SUNY or CUNY tuition after Pell, TAP and other aid ('last-dollar'); students must complete 30 credits per year and live/work in NY after graduation
programmes.deadline_note: Annual application window (typically summer); FAFSA and TAP applications also required

procedure_steps.detail: File the FAFSA and the NYS TAP application
Submit the Excelsior Scholarship application at HESC
Sign the contract agreeing to live and work in New York after graduation

eligibility.income_note: NY resident undergraduates at SUNY/CUNY with household adjusted gross income of $125,000 or less

programmes.source_snippet: The Excelsior Scholarship, in combination with other student financial aid programs, allows students to attend a SUNY or CUNY college tuition-free.

programmes.funder: New York State Higher Education Services Corporation (HESC)
programmes.amount_note: Grant toward tuition at approved New York schools; award depends on income, tuition charged, and family circumstances; does not need to be repaid
programmes.deadline_note: Apply each year by June 30 of the academic year (file the FAFSA first)

procedure_steps.detail: File the FAFSA, then complete the NYS TAP application (linked from the FAFSA confirmation page)
List your New York college choices
HESC notifies the school of your award

documents_required.doc: New York State income tax information

eligibility.income_note: New York residents attending approved in-state institutions full-time; income limits differ for dependent, independent and married students

programmes.source_snippet: TAP is a New York State grant that helps eligible residents pay tuition at approved colleges and schools in New York.

programmes.funder: New York State of Health (NY State of Health marketplace)
programmes.amount_note: $0 monthly premium and very low out-of-pocket costs for eligible lower-income New Yorkers who do not qualify for Medicaid
programmes.deadline_note: Enrollment is open year-round through NY State of Health

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through NY State of Health online, by phone or with an in-person assistor
If your income is too low for Marketplace subsidies, you are routed to the Essential Plan
Choose a plan (premium is $0 for most enrollees)

documents_required.doc: Proof of identity and NY residency

eligibility.income_note: NY residents ages 19-64 with income up to 250% of the federal poverty level who are not eligible for Medicaid or employer coverage

programmes.source_snippet: The Essential Plan offers comprehensive health insurance with no monthly premium and low out-of-pocket costs to eligible lower-income New Yorkers.

programmes.funder: Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)
programmes.amount_note: Texas's LIHEAP-funded program; helps low-income households pay electric and gas bills and addresses energy crises; benefit level set locally
programmes.deadline_note: Apply through the local community action subrecipient; funds limited

procedure_steps.detail: Find your local CEAP subrecipient agency via TDHCA's 'Help for Texans' tool
Apply with proof of income and utility bills
Payment is made to your utility provider

eligibility.income_note: Texas households with income at or below 150% of the federal poverty guidelines

programmes.source_snippet: CEAP assists low-income households in meeting their immediate energy needs, including utility payments and energy-related crisis assistance.

programmes.funder: Florida KidCare Program / Florida Healthy Kids Corporation
programmes.amount_note: Many families pay nothing; others pay a low monthly premium ($15-$20 per household for subsidized coverage) plus small copays

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online at floridakidcare.org (one application covers Medicaid, MediKids, Healthy Kids and CHIP)
The program places the child in the right component based on age and income
Pay any monthly premium and choose a plan

eligibility.income_note: Florida children through age 18 in families within the income guidelines; families above the subsidized limit can buy full-pay coverage

programmes.source_snippet: Florida KidCare offers quality, affordable health and dental insurance for children from birth through age 18.

programmes.amount_note: Refundable state credit equal to 20% of your federal Earned Income Tax Credit
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed on the Illinois income tax return (Schedule IL-E/EIC)

procedure_steps.detail: Claim the federal EITC on your federal return
File an Illinois return and claim 20% of the federal credit
Any excess is refunded

documents_required.doc: SSNs for filer and qualifying children

eligibility.income_note: Illinois residents who qualify for the federal EITC

programmes.source_snippet: The Illinois Earned Income Credit is a refundable credit equal to 20% of the federal earned income tax credit.

programmes.funder: NYC Department of Social Services / MTA
programmes.amount_note: 50% discount on subway and eligible bus fares and Access-A-Ride paratransit trips (issued as a Fair Fares OMNY card)

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online at ACCESS HRA Fair Fares or at a DSS office
Submit proof of identity, age, NYC residency and income
Receive a Fair Fares OMNY card in the mail within about three weeks

eligibility.income_note: NYC residents ages 18-64 with household income at or below 145% of the federal poverty level (e.g., $23,475 for a household of 1); not receiving another transit discount

programmes.source_snippet: Fair Fares NYC helps low-income New Yorkers save 50% on public transportation including subway fares, eligible bus fares, and Access-A-Ride paratransit trips.

programmes.name_en: Big Apple Connect (Free Internet for NYCHA Residents)
programmes.funder: NYC Office of Technology and Innovation
programmes.amount_note: Free home internet (up to 300 Mbps) plus basic cable TV, modem and router for residents of eligible NYCHA developments

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm your NYCHA development is on the eligible list
Call the provider for your development (Optimum 866-580-1410 or Spectrum 866-960-1754)
Schedule installation; bills for internet and basic cable are reduced to $0

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested; must live in an eligible NYCHA development

programmes.source_snippet: NYCHA residents in eligible developments can receive for free: internet connections with download speeds of up to 300 Mbps, wireless router, modem, and basic cable TV.

programmes.name_local: CityFHEPS (City Fighting Homelessness and Eviction Prevention Supplement)
programmes.amount_note: City pays the landlord the difference between the tenant's contribution (generally 30% of income) and the rent up to a payment standard based on household size

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through a Homebase office (in community) or your DHS shelter housing specialist
DSS determines eligibility and issues a shopping letter
Find an apartment anywhere in New York State; DSS inspects it and pays the landlord

documents_required.doc: Proof of identity for household members
Eviction notice or shelter status documentation

eligibility.income_note: Households in shelter or at risk of eviction with income up to 200% of the federal poverty level at entry

programmes.source_snippet: CityFHEPS is a rental supplement program administered by DSS that helps individuals and families in shelter or facing eviction move to or keep permanent housing.

programmes.name_en: Senior Citizen / Disability Rent Increase Exemption
programmes.amount_note: Landlord gets a property-tax abatement equal to future rent increases, so the tenant's rent is frozen at the current level in rent-regulated apartments

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility (age 62+ or disabled, rent-regulated apartment, income and rent-share limits)
Apply online or by mail to the Department of Finance
Renew periodically; rent stays frozen while the landlord receives the tax credit

eligibility.income_note: Tenants 62+ (SCRIE) or with a qualifying disability (DRIE) in rent-regulated housing with household income of $50,000 or less paying more than one-third of income in rent

programmes.source_snippet: The NYC Rent Freeze Program freezes the rent of eligible senior citizens and people with disabilities in rent-regulated apartments; landlords receive a corresponding property tax abatement.

programmes.funder: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LA Metro)
programmes.amount_note: Free or deeply discounted fares on LA Metro and participating regional transit operators for qualifying low-income riders

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility and apply online or at a LIFE enrollment event
Load the benefit onto a TAP card
Ride with free or discounted fares on participating agencies

documents_required.doc: Proof of income or participation in CalFresh, Medi-Cal or other qualifying program

eligibility.income_note: LA County residents with household income at or below the LIFE limits (around the federal poverty level), or participants in qualifying benefit programs

programmes.source_snippet: The LIFE program provides fare subsidies to low-income transit riders in Los Angeles County.

programmes.amount_note: Substantially discounted flat fares on King County Metro, Sound Transit and other Puget Sound agencies loaded on an ORCA card

procedure_steps.detail: Verify income eligibility online or at an enrollment office
Enroll and receive a free ORCA LIFT card
Load value and ride at the reduced LIFT fare; renew every two years

documents_required.doc: Proof of income or participation in Apple Health (Medicaid)/EBT

eligibility.income_note: Income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level (King, Pierce and Snohomish county residents)

programmes.source_snippet: ORCA LIFT is a reduced transit fare program for riders whose household income is at or below 200% of the federal poverty level.

programmes.name_en: San Francisco Free Muni for Youth
programmes.amount_note: All youth 18 and under ride Muni free; no application or Clipper card required (youth may use a Youth Clipper card but are not required to tag)

procedure_steps.detail: No application needed - youth 18 and under simply board Muni without paying

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested; all youth 18 and under in San Francisco

programmes.source_snippet: Free Muni for All Youth lets everyone 18 years old and younger ride Muni for free, regardless of household income.

programmes.amount_note: Low-cost home internet (50 Mbps) for about $14.95/month plus option to buy a low-cost computer; no credit check or contract

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online at internetessentials.com
Verify eligibility via a qualifying assistance program or income
Get a self-install kit and activate service

documents_required.doc: Proof of participation in a qualifying program (e.g., SNAP, Medicaid, housing assistance) or income

eligibility.income_note: Households participating in qualifying federal/state assistance programs or within Comcast's low-income eligibility rules in its service area

programmes.source_snippet: Internet Essentials provides affordable high-speed home internet to qualifying low-income households.

programmes.amount_note: Low-cost home internet plan (around $30/month) for eligible households; free installation and no annual contract

procedure_steps.detail: Check availability and apply at att.com/internet/access
Verify eligibility via SNAP, SSI or income
Schedule installation of the discounted plan

documents_required.doc: Proof of participation in SNAP or SSI, or income documentation

eligibility.income_note: Households with a member on SNAP or SSI (or income at or below 200% of federal poverty guidelines) in AT&T's wireline service area

programmes.source_snippet: Access from AT&T provides low-cost wireline home internet service to qualifying limited-income households.

programmes.amount_note: Discounted high-speed internet plan for qualifying low-income households; includes modem and no data caps

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility at spectrum.com
Provide proof of participation in a qualifying program
Sign up for the discounted plan

documents_required.doc: Proof of participation in the National School Lunch Program, CEP, SSI (65+), or other qualifying programs

eligibility.income_note: Households with a member receiving National School Lunch Program benefits, Community Eligibility Provision participation, or SSI (for applicants 65+)

programmes.source_snippet: Spectrum Internet Assist offers high-speed internet at a discounted price to eligible low-income households.

programmes.funder: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (regulated by the CPUC)
programmes.amount_note: Roughly 20% or greater discount on monthly gas and electric bills (about 30-35% on electricity and 20% on gas)

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online via your PG&E account or by paper form
Provide household size and income (or proof of participation in a qualifying program)
Discount applies automatically to future bills; renew every 2 years

documents_required.doc: Income information or benefit program proof

eligibility.income_note: Households with income at or below the CARE limits (200% of federal poverty guidelines) or enrolled in programs like Medi-Cal, CalFresh, SSI or WIC

programmes.source_snippet: CARE provides a monthly discount on energy bills for income-qualified PG&E households.

programmes.funder: Consolidated Edison (regulated by the NYS PSC)
programmes.amount_note: Monthly bill discount on electric and/or gas service for customers enrolled in qualifying government assistance programs

procedure_steps.detail: Enroll in a qualifying benefit (HEAP, SNAP, SSI, Public Assistance, etc.)
Apply with Con Edison online or by phone with proof of benefit enrollment
Discount appears on your monthly bill automatically

documents_required.doc: Proof of enrollment in a qualifying assistance program

eligibility.income_note: Con Edison customers in NYC and Westchester receiving HEAP or other qualifying means-tested benefits

programmes.source_snippet: Con Edison's Energy Affordability Program provides monthly bill discounts to customers enrolled in certain government assistance programs.

programmes.name_en: Bank On Low-Cost Certified Checking Accounts
programmes.funder: Cities for Financial Empowerment Fund (CFE Fund) with partner banks and credit unions
programmes.amount_note: Certified accounts cost $5 or less per month (many are free), have no overdraft/NSF fees, and low or no minimum opening deposit

procedure_steps.detail: Find a Bank On certified account near you at joinbankon.org
Open the account online or in branch with ID
Use direct deposit and a debit card without overdraft fees

eligibility.income_note: Open to everyone; designed for unbanked and low-income consumers

programmes.source_snippet: Bank On certified accounts are safe, affordable transaction accounts with no overdraft fees and monthly costs of $5 or less.
